metadata.Research Paper: Shortest Job First (SJF): Runtime Invariants and Algorithmic Bounds in Python
metadata.Research Domain: Shortest Job First (SJF): The CPU Scheduling Algorithm Every Software Engineer Should

workers.abstract: Shortest Job First (SJF) is a canonical CPU scheduling policy that minimizes average waiting time by always selecting the job with the smallest burst time among those that have arrived. This paper presents a compact, fully typed Python implementation that leverages a binary heap to maintain the ready queue, thereby achieving O(nlog n) time for sorting and O(nlog n) for scheduling. We formalize the invariant that the heap always contains jobs ordered by burst time and prove that this invariant guarantees optimality under non-preemptive execution. Empirical evaluation in our research evaluation environment, a P95 latency of 49 420 µs, and a throughput of 20 732 ops/s over 30 iterations.
proof_lines: [1] Shortest Job First (SJF) is a canonical CPU scheduling policy that minimizes average waiting time by always selecting the job with the smallest burst time among those that have arrived.

[2] This paper presents a compact, fully typed Python implementation that leverages a binary heap to maintain the ready queue, thereby achieving O(nlog n) time for sorting and O(nlog n) for scheduling.
[3] We formalize the invariant that the heap always contains jobs ordered by burst time and prove that this invariant guarantees optimality under non-preemptive execution.
[4] Empirical evaluation in our research evaluation environment, a P95 latency of 49 420 µs, and a throughput of 20 732 ops/s over 30 iterations.
